subject.title: fix(wechat): preserve existing accounts across hot reload

question: Should Gateway/plugin owners accept reload.accountIndexReloadPaths as a supported channel-plugin contract for externally maintained account indexes, and accept the current regression-only proof or require live WeChat evidence before merge?
rationale: The branch moves beyond a local WeChat bug fix by adding reusable plugin metadata that changes how core chooses account-preserving restarts; neither its permanent API status nor the required provider-level proof threshold can be inferred safely from source alone.

options.title: Approve contract with live proof
options.body: Accept the generic metadata direction, but require a redacted live WeChat A+B QR-login run showing account A remains online after account B is added.

options.title: Approve regression-proof waiver
options.body: Accept the metadata contract and explicitly record that the focused Gateway lifecycle suite is sufficient for this provider-backed change.

options.title: Narrow or defer the contract
options.body: Decline the new plugin metadata surface for now and ask for a smaller owner-approved approach or a separate plugin API proposal.

recommendation.title: Approve contract with live proof
recommendation.body: Accept the generic metadata direction, but require a redacted live WeChat A+B QR-login run showing account A remains online after account B is added.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent multi-account Gateway reload work makes this the strongest evidence-backed routing candidate, though final ownership should be confirmed by repository maintainers.
